item.content:encoded: The image was part of the eco movement "Green Drinks" in Auckland. As there is no evidence that shows it was released under CC 3.0, it is assumed not compliant with the site's license and has since been removed.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Given the various references to funding needs, I would be surprised if no one suggested a very controlled ongoing patch of this stuff as a source of saleable materials; both the mentioned output substances are industrially useful. Might get rejected due to the containment difficulty costing more than they could earn, or because even selling some would still eventually alter the Earth's atmosphere to a potentially significant level (albeit not a complete Xforming).

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Casually is not the right word- its more like "in very specific conditions at high enthalpies", and it only works because Xenon has so many electron shells that the outer ones aren't held in place very well.

The rest of the Noble Gases are far less cooperative- Radon only reacts with Florine (and that only at extreme enthalpies), HArF is the only known Argon compound, and helium and neon haven't been successfully reacted with anything yet.

item.content:encoded:
I hate to be a fuddy-duddy, but argon is a noble gas, and therefore inert. To say this plant gives it off as a biproduct of metabolism implies that it is capable of atomic nuclear reaction. I mean, I get that this is probably part of the anomaly, but it leaves me scratching my head.

Also, I can't tell what you mean by "argon- and cobalt-based gas". Like, is it an (impossible) ArCo molecule?

Still, I really like the SCP. So there will be no downvote for you. A chemical spill resulting in anomalous terra-forming tickles my funny bone.
